title: A whole flood, and still most did not believe.
subtitle: Nuh's story ends with a sign few accepted

row.title: proof forces belief
sub: show me and I will follow

row.title: a sign invites
sub: most still choose to look away

then: Nuh called his people for a very long time, in secret and openly. They answered with a threat to stone him. He asked Allah to judge between them, and {reward}he and the believers were saved in the laden ship{/reward} while the rest drowned. Then comes the line: {idea}in that is a sign.{/idea}
now: You have seen it happen. A friend survives a crash, a scare at the hospital, a near loss of everything. For a week they pray and call their mother. Then life returns to normal and the lesson fades. {trap}The sign was clear. The change did not last.{/trap}
old: If I saw something truly clear, I would change for good.
new: Signs are already everywhere; what is rare is a heart that keeps responding to them.
try: Think of one moment this year that shook you. Write down what it was trying to teach you.

title: Mighty enough to end it, merciful enough to wait.
subtitle: Two names closing the story of Nuh
then: Nuh's people had years of his calling before anything happened. When the end came, {idea}it was total for those who refused{/idea} and {reward}complete safety for those in the ship.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ, grieving over Makkah's rejection, hears the same two names after each story.
now: You keep a habit you know is wrong, and nothing bad has happened yet. It is easy to read that quiet as approval. {reward}The quiet is a door held open.{/reward} The same Lord who waits is also able.
old: Since nothing has happened to me, it must not matter much.
new: His patience with me is mercy, and His might means the patience is not forever.
try: Pick one thing you have been delaying to fix with Allah. Take the first small step today.

title: Denying one messenger is denying them all.
subtitle: The people of 'Ad enter the story
then: After Nuh's people came 'Ad, living in the curved sand-hills of the Ahqaf near Yemen. They were tall, strong, and richly provided for. Allah sent one of their own, Hud, to them. The verse says {trap}they denied the messengers{/trap}, plural, because {idea}every messenger carried the same call.{/idea}
now: Your father warned you about something years ago. Then a teacher said it. Then a friend. Then a stranger online. You dismissed each one separately. {idea}It was one message wearing different faces.{/idea}
old: I am only disagreeing with this one person.
new: When the same truth keeps reaching me through different people, I am answering the truth, not the person.
try: Notice one piece of advice you have heard from more than one person. Give it a fair hearing today.

title: Their brother asked: will you not be mindful?
subtitle: Hud speaks as family, not as a stranger
then: Allah sent Hud, {idea}one of their own{/idea}, to 'Ad. He opened with the same words Nuh had used with his people: a question, not a shout. {reward}Will you not have taqwa?{/reward}
now: Your cousin is sliding into something harmful. You could post a long lecture in the family group chat. Or you could sit next to him and ask one honest question. {idea}Hud chose the question.{/idea}
old: To correct someone I need to be firm and tell them they are wrong.
new: The best warning sounds like a brother asking, not a judge announcing.
try: If you need to advise someone today, start with a question instead of a statement.

title: He was a messenger they could trust.
subtitle: Hud points to his own honesty
then: Hud tells 'Ad that he is {reward}a trustworthy messenger{/reward} to them. He was one of their own, so they knew his character. The Quraysh too knew the Prophet ﷺ well, {trap}yet called him a poet and a sorcerer.{/trap}
now: A colleague who has never lied to you raises a concern about a deal everyone else loves. You brush it off because it is inconvenient. {idea}Their track record was the reason to listen.{/idea}
old: I decide whether to listen based on whether I like what I hear.
new: When someone honest brings a hard truth, their honesty is part of the evidence.
try: Think of the most honest person in your life. Ask them one thing they think you should hear.

title: Be mindful of Allah, then follow the guide.
subtitle: The order matters: Allah first, then His messenger
then: Hud's call is short: {idea}worship your Lord and obey your Messenger.{/idea} He does not ask them to follow him for himself. Obeying him is simply how mindfulness of Allah takes shape in daily life.
now: You say you fear Allah, but when guidance gets specific, about your tongue, your money, your prayer times, you start negotiating. {trap}Taqwa that never becomes action stays a feeling.{/trap}
old: As long as I respect God in my heart, the details are optional.
new: Mindfulness of Allah shows itself in following the guidance He sent.
try: Choose one specific piece of guidance you already know and follow it fully today.

title: He wanted nothing from them.
subtitle: No fee, no favor, only from the Lord

row.title: what is in it for him

then: Hud says the same line Nuh said before him: {reward}my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds.{/reward} A messenger who asks for nothing has {idea}no reason to mislead.{/idea}
now: You help your neighbor move, then quietly wait for the thank-you post, or a favor later. When it does not come, you feel cheated. {reward}Hud's reward was already booked elsewhere.{/reward}
old: If I give my time, I should get something back from people.
new: Good done for Allah is already paid; people's thanks is a bonus, not the wage.
try: Do one helpful thing today and tell no one about it.

title: Monuments on every hill, built just to show off.
subtitle: Building for amusement, not for need

row.title: wasted lives
sub: time and bodies spent on nothing

then: 'Ad built a huge, dazzling structure at each well-known crossroads. {trap}Not because they needed it, but for fun and to show off their strength.{/trap} Hud objected because it {idea}wasted time, exhausted people's bodies, and benefited no one{/idea} in this world or the next.
now: The car you financed so it would look good in the driveway. The renovation planned mostly for photos. Weekends spent on projects whose real purpose is to be seen. {idea}What is it actually for?{/idea}
old: If I can afford it, building something impressive is my business.
new: Effort spent only to be admired is effort lost, and other people often pay for it.
try: Look at one thing you are working on. Ask honestly who it is really for.

title: Building fortresses as if they would never leave.
subtitle: Strong walls do not make a person last
then: Mujahid explained these as {trap}fortresses built strong and high, structures meant to last.{/trap} They built as though they would stay forever. Ibn Kathir notes that {idea}it would not happen; they would cease, like those before them.{/idea}
now: You plan the next thirty years in detail: mortgage, retirement, the house extension. You have never once planned for the day you leave all of it. {idea}The walls will outlast you.{/idea}
old: If I build a secure enough life, I will be safe.
new: Nothing I build keeps me here; I should build for where I am going too.
try: Next to one long-term plan you have, write one plan for your akhirah.

title: When they struck, they struck like tyrants.
subtitle: Strength without mercy

row.title: how do I use it
sub: when I have the upper hand

then: Ibn Kathir describes 'Ad as {trap}strong, violent and tyrannical.{/trap} When they seized someone, they did it with no limit and no mercy. Their strength was a gift, but {idea}they turned it against people.{/idea}
now: You are the manager now. A junior makes a mistake in front of the client. You could correct them quietly, or crush them in the meeting. {idea}Power shows who you are.{/idea}
old: When I am in the right and in charge, being harsh is fair.
new: Having the upper hand is exactly when I am tested on mercy.
try: Next time you have power over someone today, a child, a worker, a waiter, choose the softer word.

title: After naming their wrongs, he asked again.
subtitle: Hud repeats his call after the warning
then: Hud has just named three things: {trap}building for show, building as if to live forever, and striking like tyrants.{/trap} Then he does not condemn them. He repeats his invitation: {idea}worship your Lord and obey your Messenger.{/idea}
now: Your friend lays out, honestly, what you have been doing wrong. The list stings. But they end with: and I know you can change. {idea}A real warning always ends with a way back.{/idea}
old: Once my faults are named, there is no point trying.
new: Naming my faults is how the invitation to return becomes specific.
try: Take one fault someone pointed out to you recently. Treat it as a direction, not a verdict.

title: Fear the One who gave you what you know.
subtitle: Hud turns from warning to reminding of gifts
then: Hud begins {reward}reminding them of the blessings Allah had given them.{/reward} He does not need to list unknown things. He points to {idea}what they already know{/idea}, what they see every day.
now: Your salary, your health, the fact that your kids woke up today. You know all of these. You have just stopped seeing them as given. {reward}You already know the list.{/reward}
old: What I have came from my own effort.
new: Everything I know I have was supplied to me, and the Giver deserves my mindfulness.
try: Before you sleep, name five things you have today that you did not create.

title: Livestock and children were His gifts.
subtitle: Wealth and family named as provision
then: Hud names the two things 'Ad valued most: {reward}their animals and their sons.{/reward} Wealth and family were their pride and their power. He reminds them that {idea}Allah is the one who aided them with both.{/idea}
now: Your child's graduation photo. Your savings slowly growing. You feel proud, and it is natural. {idea}Pride can still say: You gave me this.{/idea}
old: My family and my wealth are what I built.
new: My family and my wealth are gifts I am trusted with, not trophies I earned alone.
try: Thank Allah out loud today for one person in your family, by name.

title: Gardens and springs in the middle of sand.
subtitle: The land itself was a gift
then: 'Ad lived among sand-hills near Hadramawt, yet Ibn Kathir notes they had {reward}gardens, rivers, crops and fruits.{/reward} Hud completes the list of gifts with {idea}gardens and springs{/idea}, things they saw every day.
now: You turn on the tap and water comes out. Clean, warm if you want. You complain when the pressure is low. {reward}Somewhere today, someone walked an hour for less.{/reward}
old: Running water and green spaces are just normal.
new: What feels normal to me is provision someone else is praying for.
try: The next time you drink water today, pause and say alhamdulillah before the first sip.

title: I fear for you, said the brother.
subtitle: A warning that comes from care
then: Hud ends: {idea}I fear for you{/idea} the punishment of a great day, if you disbelieve and oppose. Ibn Kathir says he called them with {reward}words of encouragement and words of warning{/reward}, but it was to no avail.
now: Your mother keeps calling about the late nights and the skipped meals. It feels like nagging. {idea}It is fear for you, said in the only way she knows.{/idea}
old: People who warn me are trying to control me.
new: A warning can be the most loving thing someone says to me.
try: Call or message someone who has warned you about something. Thank them for caring.
